newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares edge up on local demand, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares edge up on local demand, seen steady.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed on local demand in calm morning trade on Wednesday, dealers said, predicting the Russian Trading System (RTS) 22-share index which set a record at the opening would change little over the day.
The RTS index opened at a record 526.38, a fraction above Tuesday's record 526.20 close.
"The market is a little bit stronger -- we're seeing more buyers, mostly Russian," said CS First Boston chief trader Igor Rozhkov.
He and CentreInvest Securities trader Alexander Pankov predicted leading shares would finish close to midday levels. Western investors were focused on low-liquidity shares, they said.
Traders said the market was little affected by results announced late on Tuesday of a privatisation tender of a stake in metals producer Norilsk Nickel.
A company linked to powerful Uneximbank won the 38 percent share, as generally expected by the market.
Trade in Norilsk was slow. Ordinary shares had eased to $14.90 at 0917 GMT after closing on Tuesday at $15.15. Prefs had risen to $13.400 from $12.600 at the previous close.
Oil company Noyabrskneftegaz sank to $14.50 from $16.05. The company said earlier it had approved a share issue under a programme to restructure it debts to the government.
National power company UES rose to $0.4400 from $0.4325 but traders said foreign investors, who drive the market, were looking at less liquid stocks on the second and third tiers.
Pankov said industrial companies and unlisted regional oil refineries were seeing demand. "There is money, it's just going to the less liquid shares," he said.
